paragraphs.text: Graded long-term memory for an AI assistant: S/A/B/C levels, automatic expiry, one plain JSONL file.
# dsh-journal
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that turns a plain JSONL file into a first-class `journal` tool with grade
d memory: entries carry a level, an expiry, and a review date, so a long-lived assistant can remembe
r the right things for the right amount of time — and let the rest go on its own.
## Why memory needs levels
A single undifferentiated memory file fails in two directions at once. Keep everything and the usefu
l part drowns; keep only recent things and the relationship and the standing preferences — the parts
that make an assistant feel like the same person — are exactly what gets dropped.
So every entry gets one of four levels, and the level decides its lifetime:
| level | meaning | lifetime |

| `S` | relationship, emotion, shared experience, promises | never auto-deleted; pinned |
| `A` | du

rable facts, preferences, key decisions | 365 days |
| `B` | project context, task progress | 60 day

s |
| `C` | transient details, one-off operations | 7 days |
`prune` soft-deletes expired rows into `archive/`; nothing is ever physically removed by the tool. P
inned rows are exempt.
The useful question when writing is not "is this important" but **"which of these is this, a skeleto
n or a file"** — the rules for how someone talks to you belong in `S`, the port number you debugged
yesterday belongs in `B`, and a handoff note for the next session belongs in `A` because it only nee
ds to survive until you read it.
## The tool
One tool, eight actions:
| action | does |

| `add` | write one entry (`level`, `title`, `text` required) |
| `list` | list entries, optionally

by level / status |
| `search` | substring search across title, text and tags |
| `digest` | the `S`

+ `A` summary — what a fresh session should read first |
| `stats` | counts per level, size, expire

d-but-present |
| `review` | push one entry's expiry out |
| `prune` | soft-delete everything past i

ts expiry |
| `render` | rewrite `JOURNAL.md` as a readable digest |

## Storage
One JSON object per line at `<root>/journal.jsonl`. Writes go through a temp file and a rename, so a
crash mid-write cannot tear the store. A torn trailing line on read is skipped rather than failing
d-write cannot tear the store. A torn trailing line on read is skipped rather than failing the call.
Row shape:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The format is deliberately plain. Any script that can read JSONL can read this, and any script that
can write one line can add to it.
## Install
A DeepSeek Harness plugin only receives the host packages (`@deepseek-ai/*`) when it is installed as
a **link**. An ordinary npm dependency fails to import and is silently skipped.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Configuration (in the bundle layer `cordis.patch.yml`):
| key | default | meaning |

| `root` | `D:/dsh-data/journal` (Windows) / `/dsh-data/journal` | where `journal.jsonl` lives |
| `
toolName` | `journal` | the tool's name in the model's toolset |
`JOURNAL_ROOT` overrides `root` from the environment.
## Test
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Runs against a temporary store: add at each level, list, search, digest, stats, prune dry-run, rende
r, review, and the two validation paths (bad level, empty title are both rejected).
## Note on what it is not
This is not a vector store and does not do retrieval by similarity. It is a small, inspectable, hand
-curated log — closer to a notebook than a database. The bet is that an assistant which writes down
the right few hundred lines, and forgets the rest on schedule, beats one that hoards everything and
w hundred lines, and forgets the rest on schedule, beats one that hoards everything and searches it.
